item.title: Why Young People Are Choosing Protest
item.description: Across much of the world, Gen Z-led protests have become proxies for broader discontent, fueled by deep and persistent governance failures rather than isolated events. These are not episodic flare-ups, but rather expressions of widespread frustration with the yawning gap between policy commitments and implementation.

item.title: How to Know When You’re an Empire
item.description: Despite Donald Trump's varying threats against Greenland, the United States has not yet crossed the line into empire, because Greenlandic and Danish consent still matters. Instead, it remains a hegemon that can pressure and persuade without displacing local authority.

item.title: Israel’s Emergence as an Energy Power Could Become a Liability
item.description: Although Israel’s recent deal to supply natural gas to Egypt offers many strategic and economic benefits, it also carries serious risks. Without careful planning, future Israeli governments may find themselves forced to choose between honoring export obligations and safeguarding domestic energy security.

item.title: Why Greenland Matters
item.description: The announcement of a skeletal agreement between US President Donald Trump and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte was good news, even if it turns out to be a fig leaf for a failed land grab. The brouhaha over Trump’s rhetoric was obscuring what is a genuinely serious geostrategic concern.

item.title: American or Chinese Exceptionalism?
item.description: Both US and Chinese leaders are guilty of personalizing the conflict-prone Sino-American relationship. Continuing down this path – particularly if Donald Trump’s degradation of American leadership becomes a permanent shift, rather than an aberration – raises the important question of which country is truly exceptional.

item.title: America’s Year of Self-Destruction
item.description: The United States owes its superpower status not to pure might, but to the unique combination of material advantages and Enlightenment values. With his reliance on naked power and rejection of all constraints on his authority, Donald Trump represents the opposite of everything that made the country great.

item.title: Ukraine Is Essential to Europe’s Post-American Defense
item.description: Given the growing doubts about American security guarantees, Ukraine is now the first and by far most effective line of defense for Europe. It should therefore be recognized as a key element of Europe’s defense perimeter, with access to European funding, technology, networks, and intelligence.

item.title: Trump Wants a “Hot Hot Hot” Economy
item.description: US President Donald Trump is betting that aggressive fiscal stimulus, deregulation, and looser monetary policy can deliver rapid growth without rekindling inflation. But centuries of experience across dozens of countries suggest that the kind of heterodox experiment now underway in the US rarely ends well in the long run.

item.title: Building a Middle-Power World Order
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is right to warn that the old global order has ruptured, and that middle powers must now come together to advance shared interests. They can do so by embracing the principles guiding narrower multilateral arrangements that have proved more effective than many realize.

item.title: Trump Has Condemned Europe to Success
item.description: To survive in a dangerous new world, the European Union, established as an antidote to power politics, must contradict the very principle on which it was founded by becoming a superpower in its own right. Fortunately, it already has all the assets it needs in order to do so.
